name: Enoch
charge: Walking with God three hundred years
summary: Enoch walked with God, begat sons and daughters, and was not, for God took him. Hebrews says he was translated that he should not see death and had testimony that he pleased God. Jude preserves his warning of judgment upon ungodly deeds and speeches.
offense: Enoch walked with God after the birth of Methuselah for three hundred years and begat sons and daughters (Genesis 5:21-24). The testimony describes a sustained course amid the responsibilities of a household. Walking with God was not confined to a single occasion of danger or a single offering. Jude names him as the seventh from Adam and preserves his prophecy of the Lord coming with ten thousands of his saints to execute judgment upon ungodly deeds and hard speeches (Jude 1:14-15). His walk included testimony against the evil around him. The standard was not the approval of his generation, but the judgment of the Lord he proclaimed.
judgment: Genesis says that he was not, for God took him. Hebrews explains that by faith he was translated that he should not see death, and that before his translation he had testimony that he pleased God (Genesis 5:24; Hebrews 11:5). His disappearance was not presented as failure or abandonment, but as God's taking of the faithful man. The next verse makes the principle available to the hearer: without faith it is impossible to please God, and those who come to him must believe that he rewards those who diligently seek him (Hebrews 11:6). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) calls Enoch an example of repentance to all generations (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 44:16). His particular deliverance remains God's act, while the call to seek and please God continues beyond his generation.

verses.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:
And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years:
And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints,

To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.
Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.
But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch; for he was taken from the earth.
He pleased God, and was beloved of him: so that living among sinners he was translated.
Yea speedily was he taken away, lest that wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind.
He, being made perfect in a short time, fulfilled a long time:
For his soul pleased the Lord: therefore hasted he to take him away from among the wicked.

entries.commentary: The words made he him speak of the first Adam. This Adam was made in the likeness of God, a direct descendant of the Most High. Male and female created he them, and called their name Adam: they were not that Adam; these were the other people on the earth. When the Most High creates a fish He does not create only a salmon; there is mackerel and tuna and all types of fish. In the same way, He created Adam and He created the other people. Chapter 5 is the direct lineage of Adam. That lineage is the sons of God you read of in chapter 6, and the later chapters of Genesis tie the Israelites directly to the lineage of Adam through Shem. When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam.
Enoch walked with God and was not: the Most High took him up, and Enoch did not taste death, the same way Elijah did not taste death.
Noah was five hundred years old here, and he was six hundred when the flood came ([Genesis 7:6](/bible/genesis/7#v6)), so Noah preached for around a hundred years, give or take.
